summary: UpdateChecker registers a UserDefaults.didChangeNotification observer that is never explicitly removed
detail: The preferenceObserver token is stored but deinit does not remove it. In practice UpdateChecker is effectively app-lifetime (held by ContentView @State once task 6.1 lands), and the closure captures [weak self], so no leak of interesting state occurs. If the class ever gets re-instantiated per view, add a deinit that calls NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver on the stored token. Left alone for now to avoid Swift 6 nonisolated-deinit friction on a @MainActor @Observable class.

summary: Task 5.3 implicitly required access to a UpdateChecker instance but ContentView's @State is formally introduced in task 6.1
detail: To keep the groups decoupled I placed the preference toggle in HoottyApp's .appSettings CommandGroup using @AppStorage rather than in ContentView's profileMenu, and had UpdateChecker observe UserDefaults to stay in sync. A tighter task order would put 6.1 before 5.3, or 5.3 could explicitly name the menu surface so the implementer doesn't have to balance D9 against the task-ordering constraint.
